title: Reverse Alternate Nodes and Append
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, extract all nodes at **even 1-based positions** (the 2nd, 4th, 6th, ... nodes), reverse their order, and append them to the end of the remaining odd-positioned nodes (the 1st, 3rd, 5th, ... nodes).

Return the head of the modified linked list in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Walk along the odd-positioned chain with pointer `odd`, detaching each successor `even = odd.next` as you go.
Prepend each detached `even` node to the front of a `revEven` list (`even.next = revEven; revEven = even`) so it is automatically built in reversed order, then attach `odd.next = revEven` at the end.

examples.explanation: Odd positions [10, 9, 7, 5] stay first; even positions [4, 1, 3] reverse to [3, 1, 4] and append.
Odd positions [1, 3, 5] followed by reversed even positions [4, 2] gives [1, 3, 5, 4, 2].
Odd [1, 3] followed by reversed even [4, 2] gives [1, 3, 4, 2].
